input: Negotiate my monthly internet and cable bill

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether they want to negotiate internet only, cable only, or a bundled package changes the leverage points and which services are on the table.
Whether they want to do this themselves or have coaching/a script to follow affects how the plan is structured — DIY call prep vs. delegating to a bill negotiation service.
Their current provider and how long they've been a customer determines what loyalty leverage and competitor offers they can reference.
Knowing their current monthly cost and target savings sets a concrete goal and defines what a successful negotiation looks like.
They may prioritize a lower price, a better plan, removing fees, or avoiding a contract — these require different negotiation tactics.
Whether they plan to call, use live chat, visit a store, or threaten to cancel entirely shapes the specific script and steps.
Some people are comfortable being assertive or threatening to cancel; others want a polite, low-conflict approach — this changes the tone of the negotiation script.

gold.taskTitle: Negotiate lower internet and cable bill
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to negotiate their monthly internet and cable bill to reduce costs or improve their plan terms with their provider.

questions.title: Which services are you negotiating — internet, cable, or both?
questions.description: Identify whether the negotiation covers internet only, cable only, or a bundled package, so the right services and leverage points are targeted.

questions.title: Who will actually make the call or contact the provider?
questions.description: Determine if the user wants to handle this themselves with a prepared script, get coached step-by-step, or use a third-party negotiation service.

questions.title: Who is your current provider and how long have you been a customer?
questions.description: Identify the provider and customer tenure to assess loyalty leverage and what competitor offers or retention deals may be available.

questions.title: What are you currently paying per month right now?
questions.description: Establish a baseline cost so that a realistic savings target can be set and success can be measured concretely.

questions.title: What is your primary goal — lower price, better speed, or no contract?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user's top priority is reducing the bill, upgrading their plan for the same price, eliminating fees, or avoiding a long-term contract commitment.

questions.title: How do you plan to contact your provider — call, chat, or in-store?
questions.description: Determine the contact channel so the negotiation steps and script are tailored to the format (phone call, live chat, or in-person visit).

questions.title: How comfortable are you threatening to cancel to get a deal?
questions.description: Gauge the user's willingness to use assertive tactics like cancellation threats, which are among the most effective but require a specific tone and approach.
